learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental concepts and significance of technical diagnostics.
Master non-destructive testing (NDT) techniques for assessing the technical condition of mechanical components.
Evaluate the causes of failures and predict the lifespan of machine elements based on wear symptoms.
Acquire the ability to select and operate diagnostic tools used in workshops.
Design simple systems for monitoring the technical condition of machines.
Conduct diagnostics of real mechanical systems based on actual operational data and case studies.
knows the basic techniques, methods and tools used in the technical diagnostics
can properly plan and perform tests, including measurements, interpret the obtained results, and correctly draw conclusions from them
is aware of the importance of knowledge in solving engineering problems and knows examples and understands the reasons for machines that led to serious financial, environmental and social losses

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Technical Diagnostics: significance and applications in mechanical systems
Measurement and data acquisition in diagnostics: sensor technologies and data processing methods
Selection and separation of useful signals
Analyzing machine condition through vibration and noise signals
Lubricant and Fluid Analysis in Diagnostics: methods for assessing wear and contamination in mechanical systems
Electrical system diagnostics: on-board diagnostics (OBD) and fault detection techniques
Failure Analysis and Life Cycle Prediction: identifying failure causes and estimating component lifespan
Diagnostic Equipment: modern testing instruments and software
Assessment of the technical condition of hydraulic systems
Examination of the wear of selected operating fluids in machines
Diagnostics of the onboard CAN network

assessment_methods.method: Average scores from entry tasks for laboratories
Acceptance of subsequent reports on the exercises performed by the instructor for laboratories

assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all the required learning outcomes. The lecture grade is based on the result of a test. Laboratories are graded based on the average scores from the entry tasks and the acceptance of subsequent reports on the exercises performed by the instructor.
